source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:18 ('שמות with zaqef qatan; כשמות with zaqef gadol')
claim_en: THE RE-DUG NAMES, FULL AND LEAN IN ONE VERSE: Isaac re-digs his father's wells 'and called them NAMES (שמות, plene, under zaqef qatan — the small upright accent) like the NAMES (כשמת, defective, under zaqef gadol — the great upright) his father had called them': the son's fresh namings written FULL, the father's remembered ones LEAN, each under its own upright accent exactly as ruled — restoration writes fuller than memory.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:18 (the second leg)
claim_en: ...the lean father-names under the great upright verified in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:20 ('רעי גרר — the gimel RAFEH')
claim_en: רעי גרר ('the herdsmen of GERAR strove') — the gimel soft (no doubling dot) after the vowel, as ruled.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:20 ('עשק — against Babylon, who OPPRESSED the house of Judah')
claim_en: THE QUARREL-WELL BEARS THE FRAUD-WORD: עשק ('he called the well ESEK, for they contended') — the name's consonants stand THREE times in the Torah: the well here, and twice in the fraud-laws of Leviticus ('the OPPRESSION which he committed,' Lev 5:21, 5:23): the Kitzur reads the first exile into the name (Babylon the oppressor), and the letter files the well with the Torah's own oppression-word.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:21 ('שטנה — against Haman who wrote an ACCUSATION on Jerusalem; therefore שטנה is two — here and there')
claim_en: THE ACCUSATION-WELL: שטנה ('he called it SITNAH') — UNIQUE in the Torah, and the tradition's pair-leg is the written שטנה of the exile — 'they wrote an ACCUSATION against the dwellers of Judah and Jerusalem' (Ezra 4:6; edge): the word's only other station in Scripture is the informers' letter — the Kitzur's Haman-reading rides the pair.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:22 ('רחבות — the Hilleli lean, the Jerusalem full; in ALL the books first vav lean, second full; so the Ramah')
claim_en: רחבות ('he called it REHOVOT, for now YHWH has made room') — UNIQUE in the Torah, written first-vav-LEAN second-vav-FULL exactly as all the books and the Ramah rule (the Hilleli's doubly-lean reading declined, the manuscript split named). The Kitzur reads the third kingdom into the room-well, and the escape into 'we shall be FRUITFUL in the land.'

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:22 (the spelling leg)
claim_en: ...the lean-then-full vav-pattern verified in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:22 ('ויעתק — the ayin with sheva ALONE')
claim_en: ויעתק ('and he MOVED ON from there') — the ayin with PLAIN sheva exactly as ruled, and SNAPSHOT agrees: the half-vowel split that put hataf against the rulings at four stations (the bless-word class) does NOT reach the ayin — the codex compounds only the resh and tzadi, the ayin stays bare as Minchat Shai wants it. The split is letter-specific, and this token proves the boundary.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:22 ('כי עתה — in the collations, the kaf with the lengthener for Ben Asher; in some precise books with maqqef')
claim_en: כי עתה ('for NOW YHWH has made room') — the two named camps split between the kaf-stroke (Ben Asher) and the maqqef; SNAPSHOT carries BOTH features at once (the stroke inside the joined chain): the collation-split site marked, the codex's both-marks reading filed.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:25 ('אהלו — with VAV in the precise books; NOT counted among the heh-written tents of the Noach list'; the Ramah concurs)
claim_en: אהלו ('he built an altar there... and pitched HIS TENT') — written with the closing VAV, expressly NOT one of the written-heh tent-words (the Noach-parasha ledger; frozen gen_23's אהלה crown): Isaac's tent is his own on the letter's surface — no she-tent spelling here.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:28 ('ראו — four in the Masorah, two written with vav, two with heh: the plural ones with vav, the singular with heh — for the reading follows the speaker')
claim_en: THE DOUBLED SEEING SPLITS BY SPEAKER: ראו ראינו ('we have SURELY SEEN that YHWH is with you' — the Philistines' plural confession) — the doubled see-verb's infinitive written with VAV for the plural mouth; adjacency-verified unique in the Torah...

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:28 (the singular leg)
claim_en: ...while the SINGULAR mouth writes it with HEH: ראה ראיתי ('I have SURELY SEEN the affliction of My people' — God at the bush, Exod 3:7), adjacency-verified: the Philistines' we-have-seen and God's I-have-seen, one doubled verb, two spellings, split exactly by number as the Kitzur rules.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:29 ('תעשה — the sin with TZERE')
claim_en: אם תעשה עמנו רעה ('that you will DO us no harm') — the do-verb's sin-letter in tzere as ruled.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:29 ('אתה עתה — three in the Masorah: here; YOU NOW shall make kingdom; NOW lighten the yoke — they crowned Isaac over them')
claim_en: אתה עתה ברוך יהוה ('YOU are NOW the blessed of YHWH') — the you-now pair stands ONCE in the Torah (adjacency-verified); the Masorah's legs are the kingdom-verses ('you NOW shall make kingdom,' I Kgs 21:7; 'NOW lighten the yoke,' the Rehoboam plea; edges): the Kitzur reads Gerar's greeting as a coronation.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:29 ('ברוך ה׳ — two in the Masorah as an address: here and COME, blessed of YHWH — as Laban and Bethuel intended against Eliezer, so Avimelech against Isaac')
claim_en: ...and the greeting ברוך יהוה ('blessed of YHWH') on gentile lips is the Kitzur's pair: Laban's 'COME, blessed of YHWH' to Eliezer (24:31) and Avimelech's here — the two hollow courtesies, each covering a darker intent (the poison-bowl tradition at 24:33; the 'we have not TOUCHED you' of this verse). SNAPSHOT census: the blessed-of-YHWH adjacency stands five times in the Torah — Noah's blessing (9:26), the servant's praise (24:27), Laban's greeting (24:31), Avimelech's greeting (26:29), Jethro's praise (Exod 18:10): three praises, two greetings — and both greetings are the Kitzur's pair.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:33 ('שבעה — at all the others it writes THE NAME or ITS NAME; here no name-word — for I have made you small among the nations')
claim_en: THE NAMELESS NAMING: ויקרא אתה שבעה ('he called IT Shiv'ah') — the chapter's three quarrel-wells are each named WITH a name-word (שם at Esek 26:20, שמה at Sitnah 26:21 and Rehovot 26:22, builder-asserted), but the oath-well's naming alone drops it: called IT, not called ITS NAME — the Kitzur rides the missing word into Edom's smallness-verse. The city-etymology's own שם ('therefore the NAME of the city is Beer Sheva') follows separately in the verse.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:34 ('בארי — two in the Masorah: Beeri the Hittite, and Hosea son of BEERI — who said before the Holy One: exchange them')
claim_en: בארי ('Judith daughter of BEERI the Hittite' — Esau's marriage at forty) — UNIQUE in the Torah; the Masorah's pair-leg is the prophet's father (Hos 1:1; edge): the Kitzur hangs Hosea's exchange-plea on the shared name — the Hittite father-in-law and the prophet who asked to trade Israel for another nation, answered from Esau's own line.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:35 ('ותהיין — the heh with sheva ALONE, and NO lengthener on the tav')
claim_en: ותהיין מרת רוח ('and they WERE a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and Rebecca' — Esau's wives, the chapter's last word) — UNIQUE in the Torah, the heh with plain sheva and no stroke on the tav, both as ruled: the bitterness-verse pointed bare.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:35 (the pointing leg)
claim_en: ...the bare pointing verified in the stream.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:8
claim_en: THE WELL NAMES ARE READ AS THE TABLE OF CONTENTS OF THE TORAH ITSELF. How many wells were dug? Four, matching the wilderness banners, or FIVE, matching the five books - and the naming map is laid out clause by clause: the first name is Genesis, the second Exodus, the living-water well Leviticus, the seventh-named well Numbers, and the last Deuteronomy. The count is then pushed to SEVEN by Ben Kappara's division, which treats the two traveling-Ark verses as a book in themselves and splits Numbers into three. The chain is stating the structure of its own canon and seating that structure on this block's geography.

check.note: A claim about the canon's own book-division mapped onto a narrative's place-names.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 62:3
claim_en: THE REGRESSION RULE RECORDED AT GEN_42 LANDS ITS EVIDENCE HERE. The rule that the world regressed wherever the full formula 'and it was after the death of' appears was seated at 25:11; its Abraham case is proved from THESE verses - the Philistines sealed the wells after his death - and R. Yudan's mitigation, that the world would have regressed had successors not been raised, is likewise this block's verse: Isaac dug them anew. A rule stated in one block and evidenced in the next.

check.note: A pattern rule stated at an earlier block whose proof-texts and mitigation both sit in this one.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:10
claim_en: THE CHAIN FIRES THE CANON'S OWN RESTRICTIVE-PARTICLE RULE ON THIS VERSE. From 'only good' at 26:29 the inference is drawn that their good was NOT complete - the restrictive word read as excluding rather than intensifying. The same particle-rule the machine carries elsewhere, here applied by the chain itself rather than by us, and applied against the speakers.

check.note: A restrictive-particle inference drawn by the chain, limiting a statement made in the narrative's own dialogue.

source: Onkelos Genesis 26:28
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION GIVES THE TREATY A LEGAL PAST. Where the verse has the parties propose an oath between them, Onkelos renders it as LET THE OATH THAT WAS BETWEEN OUR FATHERS NOW BE ESTABLISHED - reactivating the earlier covenant of gen_37 rather than founding a new one. An ink-level insert converting a fresh agreement into the renewal of a standing instrument.

check.note: A new agreement rendered as the reactivation of an earlier one, supplying continuity the verse does not state.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:9; Onkelos Genesis 26:26
claim_en: A NAME-OR-TITLE DISPUTE IS SETTLED BY THE OTHER MEMBER'S VOTE. R. Yehuda reads the king's companion as a proper name; R. Nechemya reads it as a COHORT OF HIS FRIENDS. Onkelos renders the cohort, siding with one party against the other without argument. The commander's name is separately parsed as a title - the mouth that all his armies kiss - the same title-parse the machine records at gen_36.

check.note: An unresolved name-versus-title dispute in which the translation casts a silent vote.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:1
claim_en: THE MARRIAGE IS GRADED AS PIETY THEATRE BY A ZOOLOGICAL SIMILE. As the pig lies down and extends its hooves to display the sign of purity it has, so an empire robs while arranging the courtroom - and so this marriage: forty years of ensnaring married women, then at forty a marriage staged in imitation of the father, because the father married at forty. The outward form of the act is read as its own disguise.

check.note: An act read as deliberate imitation staged to disguise a record, carried by an animal simile.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:2; Bereshit Rabbah 65:3
claim_en: THE MATCH IS GRADED BY TWO SEPARATE LEGAL ANALOGIES. First by the ban: let the one whose name is to be blotted marry the one whose name is to be blotted, the wives placed under the ban statute. Then by species law: the roof test in which any bird alighting beside another is judged its kind, applied to the marriage under the after-its-kind clause of the dietary law. Two different law-corpora borrowed to grade one marriage.

check.note: One marriage evaluated by a ban statute and by a species-classification rule in succession.

source: Onkelos Genesis 26:35
claim_en: THE WIVES' BITTERNESS IS CONVERTED INTO DISOBEDIENCE. Where the verse says they were a bitterness of spirit to the parents, Onkelos renders them REBELS AND AGGRAVATORS AGAINST THE WORDS of Isaac and Rebecca - a feeling in the parents becoming a fault in the wives, and an emotional description becoming a charge of defying instruction.

check.note: An emotional state of the parents rendered as an offence committed by others.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 65:4
claim_en: WHY THE FATHER IS NAMED FIRST IN THE BITTERNESS VERSE IS ANSWERED THREE WAYS. Because he was fastidious about idolatry's filth; because the matter hung on HER, the oracle at 25:23 having been spoken to her; or because his dimmed eyes kept him at home. R. Yehoshua ben Levi adds that Esau caused the Divine Spirit to depart from his parent - which wires this verse to the dimming dossier that opens gen_46.

check.note: A word-order question answered three ways, one leg reaching back to an oracle and one forward to the next block.

source: Onkelos Genesis 26:25; Bereshit Rabbah 87:5
claim_en: THE ALTAR SCENE IS CONVERTED INTO PRAYER, AND THE NIGHT REVELATION JOINS A CENSUS. Onkelos renders 'called in the name of the LORD' as PRAYED in the name of the LORD, the standing policy that writes worship vocabulary into proclamation verses. Separately, 26:24's appearance 'that night' enrols the verse in the night-revelation census the chain maintains across the corpus.

check.note: A proclamation rendered as prayer, and a revelation classed by its time of day into a standing census.
